data.traefik:
# Traefik reference config for webtop, generated by the hub from its image.yml.
# Labels for the webtop service in your compose file. Traefik's docker provider must reach the webtop
# container on a shared network; the entrypoint websecure and the certificate resolver letsencrypt are
# examples from a typical Traefik setup. Replace example.com with your domain. Websockets need nothing extra.
services:
  webtop:
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.services.webtop.loadbalancer.server.port=3001
      - traefik.http.services.webtop.loadbalancer.server.scheme=https
      # The app serves a self-signed certificate: define a serversTransport with insecureSkipVerify: true
      # in Traefik's file provider (named insecure here) and reference it.
      - traefik.http.services.webtop.loadbalancer.serverstransport=insecure@file
      - traefik.http.routers.webtop.rule=Host(`webtop.example.com`)
      - traefik.http.routers.webtop.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.webtop.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
      - traefik.http.routers.webtop.service=webtop
      # Authentication: uncomment one; the middleware is defined in your Traefik config.
      # - traefik.http.routers.webtop.middlewares=authelia@docker
      # - traefik.http.routers.webtop.middlewares=authentik@docker
